newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rwandans to study S.Africa's truth commission.
newsitem.headline: Rwandans to study S.Africa's truth commission.

text.p: A six-member Rwandan government delegation will arrive in South Africa on Sunday to study the country's efforts to heal the wounds of apartheid, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission said on Friday.

A statement said the South African commission would host the Rwandans, headed by Labour and Social Affairs Minister Pie Mugabo, during their week-long stay. In 1994 Rwandan Hutu mobs and militias slaughtered some 800,000 minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates in the country.
"They wish to obtain technical knowledge which may be useful to them in their attempts to come to terms with the gross violations of human rights which occurred in their country," the statement said.

The Rwandans, including Justice Minister Faustin Nteziryayo and Public Prosecutor Simeon Rwagasore, would discuss issues relating to national unity and reconciliation and would explore areas of future cooperation.

President Nelson Mandela set up the truth commission to obtain as full a picture as possible of political crimes and human rights violations during the apartheid era. The hope is that disclosure and confession will lead to catharsis and reconciliation.
